key_idea: Count the outcomes per sum by convolving the dice one at a time, then sort sums by count; counts reach about 2^155 so they need exact big integers rather than doubles.
sketch: DP over dice: f[s] = number of ways to reach sum s, adding one die at a time (at most 50 dice, max sum 500), about 50*500*20 additions. The total number of outcomes is up to 4^10*6^10*8^10*12^10*20^10, roughly 2^155, so use a fixed 192-bit unsigned integer (three 64-bit limbs with add and compare); floating point could misorder close but unequal counts. Print sums from (number of dice) to (max sum) sorted by non-increasing count. Ties may be printed in any order, so the sample checker reports mismatches; verified with an independent Python bigint validator (output is a permutation of all reachable sums and counts are non-increasing) on the samples, extremes like 10 10 10 10 10, and 40 random inputs.
